transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well... I guess I'm just here because I need someone to listen. It's... it's been going on for months now. My husband's family, they're... they're doing things. Quietly messing with our money, our good name. Like, I'll see these little billing errors at work, or... or someone at church will just act funny toward me out of nowhere. And I just know it's them. No matter what kind of records anyone tries to pull up to say otherwise, I know it all ties back to them. I just... I need someone to understand that.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or whispering when there was no one around to make them?
No. No, nothing like that. Just... just what I told you.
Have you recently experienced any new physical health problems or been diagnosed with any medical conditions?
No. Um... no, I haven't. Physically, I'm... I'm fine.
Before these past few months, did you generally find it hard to trust people throughout your adult life?
No. I mean, not really. I've always just kept to myself, mostly. Just... normal, I guess. I didn't have any problems before this started.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits non-bizarre, fixed persecutory delusions regarding her in-laws covertly targeting her finances and reputation, persisting unshakeably despite contrary evidence for several months. Prominent auditory hallucinations are absent, organic medical etiology is denied, and there is no lifelong premorbid pattern of pervasive paranoia, ruling out paranoid personality disorder and schizophrenia in favor of delusional disorder.
